claim: Doubly charged scalars (type-II seesaw / triplet) in compressed-spectrum cascades, long-lived (0.1-100 mm) regimes, and tau / W+W+ / H+W* final states are not covered by existing CMS/ATLAS searches, which assume prompt H++ -> e/mu pairs.
surviving_gap: (i) Fermiophobic H++ -> W+W+ with c*tau ~0.1-100 mm (m ~150 GeV to ~TeV): same-sign / charged-parent displaced-vertex search (no CMS/ATLAS result found; the ATLAS displaced-dilepton-vertex search requires opposite charge). (ii) Compressed triplet (Delta M ~1-30 GeV, H0/A0 -> nu nu) with soft low-m_ll same-sign leptons + ISR: phenomenology only, and existing compressed-electroweakino searches were shown by a recast to be insensitive. (iii) Hadronic-tau H++ final states with full Run 2/Run 3/HL data: CMS has only a 12.9 fb-1 PAS, ATLAS uses e/mu only. The prompt W+W+ channel and stable/HSCP regime are DEAD (covered).

claim: Light ALPs (10 MeV-10 GeV) with photon couplings are open: (a) in a+gamma at very high pT, where the ALP's photons fully merge into one photon candidate (0.1-6 GeV), and (b) in VBF production. Both need dedicated merged-photon substructure / conversion reconstruction plus Run-3 VBF parking or Phase-2 L1 scouting.
surviving_gap: Only the experimental execution survives. (a) A CMS/ATLAS high-mass diphoton (m_gg > ~1.5 TeV) analysis that reinterprets one photon as a merged a->gg candidate (loose+tight photon ID or shower-shape substructure), as an ALP-photon EFT limit. (b) The actual VBF-parked Run-3 / Phase-2 L1-scouting merged-conversion search, plus the invariant-mass reconstruction in the scouting stream that 2609.22570 left as future work. Both have published HL-LHC sensitivity projections already, so the 'HL-LHC projection' value-add is largely pre-empted.

showstoppers: a+gamma: Belle II at 50 ab-1 is projected to overtake the HL-LHC; for c_W ~ c_B, B->Ka already dominates. VBF scouting: the K_L -> gg long-lived background is irreducible without mass reconstruction (2609.22570 abstract), and the L1 scouting stream lacks offline-quality photons. Photon-conversion probability (~tens of %) cuts the rate.

claim: Mixed/asymmetric exotic Higgs final states lack dedicated searches: h->aa->(mumu)(gg) / 2mu4gamma, h->aa->(gg)(gamma gamma) with m_a~10 GeV, non-resonant gg->aa->4gamma at low m_a, h->Za with a->hadrons/taus/bb, and h->aa->4tau in di-Higgs production.
surviving_gap: (i) h->aa->(mu mu)(gamma gamma) with both pairs resonant at the same m_a (and 2mu4gamma contact topologies): proposed-not-searched, but motivated only where BR(a->gg) ~ BR(a->mumu). (ii) h->aa->(gg)(gamma gamma) for m_a ~10-20 GeV, where the gg system is one wide 2-prong jet, below the 20 GeV floor of the dedicated ATLAS/CMS gamma-gamma-jj / bb-gamma-gamma searches. Topical because of the CMS 13.6 GeV diphoton local excess. (iii) h->Za with a->tau tau or a->bb (m_a > 3.5 GeV), and displaced hadronic a. DEAD: h->Za(gamma gamma), h->Za(hadronic, 0.5-3.5 GeV), the generic 'h->Za not studied experimentally' claim, and HH->4tau(+bb) as an HL-LHC analysis (already projected and rate-limited).

showstoppers: HH->4tau: sigma(HH) is roughly 1/1000 of single Higgs, so it is never competitive with single-Higgs h->4tau for BR(h->aa). This part DIES as an HL-LHC analysis idea. 2mu2gamma: generic ALP models give BR(a->gg) >> BR(a->mumu) or the reverse; the mixed channel is optimal only in a narrow coupling ratio, and existing 4mu / 4gamma / Z(ll)a(gamma gamma) searches constrain the extremes. (gg)(gamma gamma) at 10-20 GeV: the low-pT wide jet faces huge gamma-gamma+jet background, and diphoton trigger thresholds hurt at m_a ~10 GeV. Non-resonant gg->aa->4gamma at low m_a: the photons merge (pairs of photon-jets) and the dim-6 rate is suppressed.

claim: HL-LHC precision timing layers (CMS MTD / ATLAS HGTD) can make displaced vertices 4D (space+time), and add time-of-flight to slow charged LLPs (HSCP). The candidate claims no CMS/ATLAS analysis or projection exploits this for DVs, delayed photons or HSCPs.
surviving_gap: Only a marginal residual survives: (i) ATLAS HGTD (2.4<|eta|<4) timing for forward LLP decay products, since the ATLAS HGTD TDR contains no LLP timing study; physics value is limited because forward tracker DVs are rare. (ii) Converting the CMS MTD TDR generator/simplified LLP studies into a full-simulation Phase-2 projection for specific benchmarks such as VBF h->ss->bb DVs with track-level timing (arXiv:2608.27868), scotogenic delayed DVs (INSPIRE:3188833) or compressed DM (arXiv:2608.29275). This is an incremental benchmark extension, not a gap in the concept.

kill_evidence.what: The TDR abstract states MTD 'provides new capabilities ... for the search for long-lived particles'. Sec. 5.4.2.1 'Vertex time discrimination and mass reconstruction of SUSY particles' uses the space-time displacement between primary and displaced e+e- vertex (GMSB neutralino -> Z gravitino, ctau 3-100 mm, 30 ps per-track time) to measure beta_LLP and reconstruct a peaking LLP mass: exactly the '4D displaced vertex' concept
Delayed photons from long-lived neutralinos timed with MTD (converted photons) + PV time: a sensitivity study at 30 ps
kill_evidence.location: Sec. 5.4.2 'Measurement of late photon with respect to the primary vertex in SUSY models', Fig. 5.27

kill_evidence.what: H -> XX -> jjjj long-lived scalar with MTD jet time relative to PV: BR(H->XX) upper limits vs lifetime (covers the h->ss, s->bb/jj delayed-DV benchmark)
HSCP velocity (1/beta) with MTD: tighter 1/beta threshold (1.25 -> 1.05) and HSCP mass reconstruction (432 GeV stau). Covers the 'timing-assisted HSCP' seed
kill_evidence.location: Sec. 'Particle velocity reconstruction in the context of HSCP searches' (p.231), Figs. 5.30-5.31
